common_name: Malaga Violet Radish (French Purple-Skinned Spring Radish)

planting.note: Direct sow as early as soil can be worked in spring or 4-6 weeks before first fall frost; Malaga Violet is a French heirloom radish with striking violet-purple skin, white flesh, and a slightly milder flavor than many spring radishes.

directions: Sow directly 1/4 inch deep as early as soil can be worked; thin to 2 inches apart. Malaga Violet is a classic French heirloom radish valued for its striking, uniform violet-purple skin over crisp white flesh, a distinctive color that stands out clearly from the more common all-red or bicolor spring radishes. The round to slightly oval roots have a clean, mild, only lightly peppery flavor, and the purple skin holds its color well even as the radish sizes up, unlike some varieties that fade. Like all spring radishes, it bolts rapidly in summer heat and should be grown only in cool weather; in zone 9, fall and very early spring are the practical growing windows. Harvest promptly once roots reach about an inch in diameter, since radishes left too long in the ground become pithy and hollow; succession-sow every two to three weeks for a continuous supply.

common_name: Amethyst Radish (Bright Purple Uniform Spring Radish)

planting.note: Direct sow as early as soil can be worked in spring or 4-6 weeks before first fall frost; Amethyst is a spring radish with smooth, bright purple skin and crisp white flesh, bred for uniform round shape and reliable color.

directions: Sow directly 1/4 inch deep as early as soil can be worked; thin to 2 inches apart. Amethyst is a modern spring radish bred for uniform, smooth, round roots with bright, consistent purple skin and crisp white interior, offering reliable color and shape for gardeners and market growers who want a purple radish that performs predictably. Flavor is mild and clean, similar to other fast-maturing spring radish types, without the excess pepperiness that develops in some varieties left too long in the ground. Like all spring radishes, it bolts rapidly in summer heat and should be grown only in cool weather; in zone 9, fall and very early spring are the practical growing windows. Harvest promptly once roots reach about an inch in diameter, and succession-sow every two to three weeks for a continuous supply.

common_name: Rudolf Radish (Extra-Early Bright Red Spring Radish)

planting.note: Direct sow as early as soil can be worked in spring or 4-6 weeks before first fall frost; Rudolf is one of the fastest-maturing spring radishes available, producing smooth, bright red, round roots in as little as three weeks.

directions: Sow directly 1/4 inch deep as early as soil can be worked; thin to 2 inches apart. Rudolf is bred for extremely fast maturity, often ready to harvest in as little as three weeks from sowing, among the quickest radishes available, making it an excellent choice for gardeners wanting the fastest possible turnaround or squeezing in an extra succession planting before summer heat arrives. Roots are smooth, round, and bright cherry-red with crisp white flesh and a clean, mild flavor typical of quick-maturing spring radishes. Because it matures so fast, timing the harvest promptly is especially important, since even quick radishes turn pithy and hollow if left in the ground too long after reaching full size. Like all spring radishes, it bolts rapidly in summer heat and should be grown only in cool weather; in zone 9, fall and very early spring are the practical growing windows.

common_name: De 18 Jours Radish (Classic French Ultra-Fast Radish)

planting.note: Direct sow as early as soil can be worked in spring or 4-6 weeks before first fall frost; De 18 Jours ('of 18 days') is a classic French heirloom radish named for its remarkably fast maturity, among the quickest radishes traditionally grown.

directions: Sow directly 1/4 inch deep as early as soil can be worked; thin to 2 inches apart. De 18 Jours, French for 'of 18 days,' is a classic heirloom radish named for its exceptionally fast maturity, historically prized by French market gardeners for getting a crop to harvest faster than almost any other vegetable. Roots are small, round to oval, bright red, and crisp, with a clean, mild flavor typical of quick spring radishes when harvested promptly at the right size. Because it matures so quickly, it is well suited to intercropping between slower-growing vegetables or squeezing in an extra succession planting in a short cool window. Like all spring radishes, it bolts rapidly in summer heat and should be grown only in cool weather; in zone 9, fall and very early spring are the practical growing windows, and succession sowing every two weeks keeps a steady supply coming.
